releases.title: Artists for Peace and Justice Gala Celebrates 18 Years of Impact During Toronto Film Festival, Celebrating Andrea Martin, Emily Hampshire and Jann Arden
releases.body:
APJ raises over $700,000 to support education and community-led initiatives in Haiti

TORONTO, Sept. 14, 2026 /CNW/ -- Board Chair Natasha Koifman and powerhouse board members George Stroumboulopoulos, Kardinal Offishall, Amanda Brugel and more, hosted the 18th annual Artists for Peace and Justice (APJ) Gala this evening at the Windsor Arms Hotel, the landmark venue that hosted the organization's first Toronto gala. Recognized as one of the city's most anticipated philanthropic events, the gala raised over $700,000 to support education and community-led initiatives in Haiti.

Since its founding, APJ has raised over $37 million and supported more than 32,000 students through access to quality education, healthcare, and opportunity.

The evening honoured three remarkable women whose careers and philanthropy embody the spirit of Artists for Peace and Justice: Andrea Martin, Emily Hampshire and Jann Arden.

Natasha Koifman, Chair of the Board, opened the evening with remarks on APJ's evolving mission, from rebuilding after the 2010 earthquake to using education as a lifeline for children caught in Haiti's escalating gang crisis today. "Believing in a better future is no longer enough. We have to be the lifeline that helps pull these children out of danger. The situation in Haiti has changed dramatically since APJ was founded, and while we haven't been able to return to the country because of the ongoing crisis, our commitment to the children we serve has never wavered. Today, education is not just about preparing young Haitians to rebuild their country in the future - it is a lifeline in the present, giving children a safe place to learn, hope, and build a path beyond the violence. The humanitarian crisis and the daily struggle to survive are unimaginable, and that makes our work more urgent than ever."

Evening Highlights

  • Setting the tone for the night, a buzzy red carpet welcomed a special group of guests: adoptable puppies from Project Paws, who posed for photos with talent and guests to help spotlight pets in need of a home.
  • APJ Board Members George Stroumboulopoulos and Kardinal Offishall returned as emcees for the evening, welcoming guests and expressing gratitude for the continued generosity that fuels APJ's mission.
  • Rick Mercer, a past APJ Award recipient, presented Emily Hampshire with the Canadian Artists for Peace and Justice Changemaker Award, celebrating her work using her platform to raise awareness around mental health and queer experiences. Hampshire's Schitt's Creek co-star Noah Reid took the stage after to perform a special song in her honour.
  • Amanda Brugel, last year's Changemaker Award recipient and a new APJ board member, presented Jann Arden with the Artists for Peace and Justice Impact Award, in recognition of her decades-long commitment to philanthropy, humanitarian causes and giving back to communities in need.
  • George Stroumboulopoulos presented Andrea Martin with the Global Artists for Peace and Justice Award, honouring her longstanding commitment to humanitarian causes and her dedication to creating positive change. Martin surprised the room with an impromptu rap after accepting the honour.
  • Norman Gaudet, former head of the Toronto French School, took the stage to announce an extraordinary milestone: inspired by Wes Hall, he created a full international scholarship after discovering APJ's mission last year. He proudly shared that Schnaider, the Academy's scholarship recipient, has officially arrived in Canada and is settling in with his host family, a testament to the importance of giving these children new opportunities outside of Haiti.
  • The live auction, led by The Auctionista, was one of the night's most electric moments, as guests bid fast and furiously on an extraordinary collection of art. Celebrated artists Russell Young, Tyler Shields and Mr. Brainwash, courtesy of Taglialatella Gallery, along with Anthony Ricciardi, saw their work draw serious heat in the room. Young, in attendance for the evening, unveiled a truly one-of-a-kind charitable commission: a family portrait shot by CAFA winner Renata Kaveh and rendered in his signature diamond dust technique, destined to become a cherished heirloom for its new owner.
  • The energy hit a fever pitch over a rare Birkin, courtesy of Carly Jordan, sparking a spirited bidding war between guests determined not to leave empty-handed. Also up for grabs: travel packages from Air Canada, a culinary evening at Michelin-starred Enigma Yorkville, and two once-in-a-lifetime experiences, the Bautista Impact Summit in the Bahamas and a getaway to Hightail Ranch in Montana.
  • Mandy Rennehan and Lauren Ferraro led a lively final Fund the Need moment, courtesy of Dean Davidson, with guests raising their hands to purchase 20 special bracelets to support some of the highest-need areas of APJ's Academy for Peace and Justice.
  • Haitian music icon and long-time APJ supporter Paul Beaubrun closed the night with an emotional performance.

Generous sponsors for this year's event include: Air Canada, 2Fifteen by DBS Developments, Audi, and Forest Hill Group.

Download Images here –  Credit Shutterstock Images (Photographers: Tyler Da Silva/ and Ernesto DiStefano)

ABOUT ARTISTS FOR PEACE AND JUSTICE

Artists for Peace and Justice (APJ) is a non-profit organization that encourages peace and social justice and addresses issues of poverty around the world. APJ's immediate goal is to serve the poorest communities in Haiti with programs in education, healthcare, and dignity through the arts. The organization is committed to long-term, sustainable development in direct partnership with the Haitian people. APJ partners with St. Luke's Foundation in Haiti. To learn more, visit www.apjnow.org or follow @artistsforpeace on Instagram and Twitter.

ABOUT NKPR

NKPR was started in 2002 by Natasha Koifman to combine two passions: shining a spotlight on stories of substance and supporting causes that are making a difference around the world. Over the past 24 years, NKPR has established itself as a highly regarded full-service public relations, artist management and digital agency with offices in Toronto, New York and Los Angeles, representing over 40 national and international brands and supporting charitable organizations like Artists for Peace and Justice. For more information, visit NKPR on social media @natashankpr or at www.nkpr.net.

releases.title: ALPHA CENTAURI Arrives As Hip-Hop's Next Rising Star With Debut Album 'The Future Right Now'
releases.body:
LinkTree I Spotify I YouTube I Website I Facebook I Instagram I TikTok

VANCOUVER, BC, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- After five years of work, six singles, and a rollout that has steadily built him into one of the most electrifying new voices on the West Coast, ALPHA CENTAURI is here with his full debut album, 'The Future Right Now,' out now via Rogue Planet. "Never Be," "Grow," "Get Your Money Up," "I'll Fly," "Higher Up" and "We Rise" each landed with their own moment in the spotlight. The ten-track album is a genre blending, funk soaked, Afrobeat charged, jazz-tinged hip-hop statement recorded entirely live off the floor with his eight-piece band.

ALPHA's own story is exactly the kind that makes a debut like this hit harder. Trained and licensed as a lawyer in Zimbabwe, he walked away from a secure, respected career to chase the thing he could never actually let go of, music. It started long before law school, back when he was 13 years old breakdancing with his crew, Blade Squad, at pageants and basketball halftime shows. "I took what I understood from dancing, rhythm and movement, and turned it into rap," he says. "I tapped into my background in English literature and realized, I know how to write poems. I understand rhythm. Maybe I can do this."

'The Future Right Now' is built entirely around that idea: self belief as fuel, motivation as philosophy, the present moment as the only place the future actually gets built. "Everything I do today, everything I did all these years, has brought me here, because my future was always in the present," ALPHA says. "We Rise," was originally written back in 2014 while he was finishing his law degree. "Expect Us" channels real testimony, drawn directly from ALPHA's own experience as a practicing lawyer in Zimbabwe supporting the movement built by activist Evan Mawarire against corruption and injustice. And "Never Be" is a full display of technical firepower, stacking wordplay, literary references and mythology into bars built to be replayed just to catch everything packed inside them.

releases.body:
Spotify I YouTube I Instagram I TikTok

TORONTO, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Toronto-based producer, DJ, and beatmaker Ladji Mouflet unveils "Hatuey," a warrior of a single that pulls its title and its spirit from one of Caribbean history's most defiant figures. Built on the hypnotic percussion and rolling low end that have become his signature, the track finds Ladji at his most physical, a record made for the dance floor that carries something much older underneath it.

The name is not incidental. Hatuey was a Taino Indigenous chief who led resistance against the Spanish conquistadors in the sixteenth century and was burned at the stake for it, choosing defiance rather than surrender. Through his mother's lineage, Ladji carries Taino heritage himself, and the parallel is intentional: a song about refusing to bend. The connection runs through the visuals too, with cover art weaving together Taino imagery and the tribal tattoos Ladji and his brother wear in tribute to that history.

Ladji built "Hatuey" the way he builds everything: alone in the studio at first, composing, producing, and arranging every layer himself before bringing in his family, team and label. The result sits at the intersection of baile and the wider electronic sounds he has spent years refining, hypnotic Afro percussion set against sleek, modern production.

That sound was shaped long before Ladji touched a fader. Raised between Harlem, the South Bronx and the Lower East Side of New York, he grew up inside a household built around rhythm. His mother, from the Dominican Republic, danced salsa on stages alongside Tito Puente and Celia Cruz. His father, Senegalese and Martinican, founded a dance and music school blending West African tradition with ballet and jazz.

That sound has already found a massive audience without a major. Ladji's breakout single "Baiana 2022" has passed 35 million streams and became an unofficial anthem of the last World Cup, shared by Tom Brady, Lamine Yamal and Wayne Rooney. "French Bossa Nova" followed with more than 44 million streams. Today Ladji reaches 1.5-2.2 million monthly listeners on Spotify and more than 350,000 followers across social platforms, all built independently through his own label, Alkebulan Records.

"Hatuey" arrives as the first single from Ladji's upcoming album, 'The Pilgrimage,' a journey back to himself, tracing his roots one track at a time and letting that heritage lead the record.

releases.title: As Live Nation Enters Its Busiest Week of the Year, New Global Report Reveals a Return to Real
releases.body:
New research spanning tens of thousands of fans worldwide explores why real-world experiences are gaining value as more of life moves online.

NEW YORK, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- This week, millions of fans will compare set-list predictions as merch lines wrap around venues and restaurants and bars fill before the show. Once the lights go down, they will share an experience that can only happen live.

In the U.S., it is expected to be the busiest week for Live Nation's fan attendance this year. The milestone reflects a much larger cultural shift playing out around the world. As more of life moves online, people are placing greater value on experiences that feel unmistakably real.

The Return to Real, a new global report from Live Nation for Brands, examines what is driving that shift and what it means for culture, commerce and brands. Drawing on multiple surveys of tens of thousands of fans worldwide, the research found that 93% of fans crave real experiences over digital ones, while 80% would rather spend on experiences than on things. Live music emerged as the world's favorite form of entertainment.

As technology becomes more deeply woven into everyday life, it is getting harder to tell what was made by a person, what was generated and what actually happened. At a concert, there is no question. The artist is on stage. You are in the room. Thousands of other people are experiencing the same thing alongside you.

"People can do almost everything from their phones now," says Russell Wallach, Global President, Live Nation Media & Sponsorship. "That's exactly why the things worth leaving home for matter more than ever. The brands building lasting loyalty are becoming part of those experiences."

For brands, that opportunity comes at an interesting moment for loyalty. While 66% of fans say they engaged with loyalty programs more than a year ago, 64% say they feel less loyal to brands, and 71% say loyalty programs feel the same. More than 9 in 10 say live music benefits would make them sign up for or switch loyalty programs.

Brands across industries are already responding.

Reserved by Spotify is using its digital platform to connect fans with live experiences. "There's just no replacement for the live music experience," says Jon Ostrow, Spotify's Head of Business Development, Live Music. "Obviously, we're a digital platform, and we've got thousands who are thinking deeply daily about how to create a more robust digital environment, but we're starting to see how digital and live can go hand in hand, creating a better experience both offline and online."

Mastercard sees exclusive access becoming a new form of loyalty. "As people place greater value on real-world experiences, access has become one of the most powerful forms of loyalty," says Monica Biagiotti, EVP, Global Consumer Marketing and Sponsorships. "Whether it's traveling to experience a bucket-list concert, discovering a new destination through music, or sharing an unforgettable night with friends and family, these experiences create lasting memories. Through the Priceless Platform and our partnership with Live Nation, we're making those moments more accessible for millions of cardholders around the world."

Lowe's is extending loyalty beyond the store. "Products may bring someone through the door, but experiences are often what make them want to come back," says Amanda Bailey, VP of Customer Marketing and Loyalty. "Music connects people through emotion. Almost everyone has a song, an artist or a concert that means something to them. Live music gives us a chance to surprise and delight our loyalty members with experiences and benefits that make those moments even better."

Across industries, brands are finding new ways to make live experiences part of how they build customer relationships. The Return to Real explores what fans value about experiences they can see, feel and share for themselves, and what that shift means for brands.

Download The Return to Real here.

About Live Nation Entertainment

Live Nation Entertainment (NYSE: LYV) is the world's leading live entertainment company comprised of global market leaders: Ticketmaster, Live Nation Concerts and Live Nation Media & Sponsorship. For additional information, visit www.livenationentertainment.com.

OJAI, Calif., Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Laurel Springs School, a private, accredited pioneer of K-12 online education, today announced its partnership with New York Film Academy (NYFA), a provider of hands-on education in film, media, and performing arts. Laurel Springs School and NYFA share a mutual commitment to helping students reach their creative goals while pursuing academic excellence.

The collaboration will create new opportunities for Laurel Springs students to connect with NYFA faculty and industry experts while exploring pathways in the creative arts, including filmmaking, acting, animation, game design, musical theatre, and other visual and performing arts disciplines.

"We see tremendous alignment with Laurel Springs and its students who are already thinking differently, creating boldly, and pursuing big ambitions," said Michael Young, President and CEO at the New York Film Academy. "We're excited for this partnership to create even more opportunities for them to discover just how far their talent can take them."

Students will have access to academic, cultural, and artistic exchange experiences, including:

  • Campus experiences including field trips, tours, and hands-on activities
  • Industry and career connections with NYFA faculty and creative professionals
  • Scholarship opportunities for Laurel Springs students
  • Preferred program access, including exclusive discounts

"NYFA faculty bring real-world experience from Hollywood and independent film and television productions, the Broadway stage, and the worlds of animation, game design, and emerging media directly into the classroom. That hands-on, industry-focused approach is at the heart of the NYFA experience, and is what drew many to study with us, including Aubrey Plaza, Bill Hader, Issa Rae, filmmaker and actor Curry Barker, Marvel director Mohamed Diab, and Oscar-winning cinematographer James Friend."

"At NYFA, students don't just study the creative industries; they learn from the people actively shaping them," Young said.

Since its founding in 1991, Laurel Springs' flexible online model has served young actors and performers balancing education with professional careers, with notable alumni including Kristen Stewart, Jennifer Love Hewitt, and Josh Hutcherson. Laurel Springs' flexible academic model complements NYFA's hands-on approach, connecting students with faculty who actively work in film, media, and the performing arts.

"Our students choose Laurel Springs in part because they want the flexibility to pursue their interests and ambitions," said Marissa Draeger, Director of Partnerships at Laurel Springs. "Our partnership with New York Film Academy creates exciting new ways for students interested in the creative arts to connect their academic experience with experiential learning and learn from mentors and leaders in the industry."

To learn more about partnering with Laurel Springs, visit the Laurel Springs partnerships page.

releases.title: Agog-Supported Works Win Two of Three Immersive Prizes at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival
releases.body:
Out of the Ashes receives the Venice Immersive Special Jury Prize and Empire at Sea receives the Venice Immersive Achievement Prize; the two projects offer distinct approaches to climate storytelling

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Two projects supported by Agog: The Immersive Media Institute won two of the three prizes awarded today in the Venice Immersive competition at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival. Out of the Ashes, co-directed by Rory Mitchell and Nonny de la Peña, received the Venice Immersive Special Jury Prize. Empire at Sea, created and directed by Peter Flaherty, earned the Venice Immersive Achievement Prize.

The awards celebrate two distinct approaches to climate storytelling. Out of the Ashes is a virtual-reality documentary about loss, memory, resilience, and rebuilding after the January 2025 Los Angeles fires. Empire at Sea is an interactive solarpunk augmented-reality drama that asks audiences to confront questions of sustainability, migration, inclusion, and collective survival.

Agog-Supported Works Win Two of Three Immersive Prizes at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival

"Wendy Schmidt and I founded Agog on the belief that immersive media can bring people closer to urgent issues and help them imagine what change could look like," said Chip Giller, co-founder and executive director of Agog. "At Venice, we saw creators expand what these emerging technologies can do—and audiences responded in deeply personal ways. Out of the Ashes brought people from around the world close to the human toll of the Los Angeles fires, and many saw echoes of what their own communities have experienced. Empire at Sea shows new possibilities for filmmaking by pairing cinematic performance and an accomplished cast with the power of immersive media. Seeing both works recognized on a global stage makes us more excited than ever about immersive media's potential to advance storytelling, contribute to social change, and serve the public good."

"Out of the Ashes and Empire at Sea are ambitious, deeply human works that demonstrate the creative range of immersive storytelling," said Liz Rosenthal and Michel Reilhac, curators of Venice Immersive. "Agog made a meaningful contribution to Venice Immersive this year, not only through its support of three projects selected for competition, but also by creating spaces where artists, producers, technologists, and changemakers could experiment, exchange ideas, and form new connections. That combination of supporting individual projects and investing in the wider ecosystem is exactly what an emerging field needs to grow."

About Out of the Ashes

Narrated by award-winning actor Courtney B. Vance, Out of the Ashes places audiences within the events and aftermath of the Los Angeles wildfires. The 26-minute documentary combines first-person storytelling with volumetric reconstructions of participants' homes, created in part from their own family photos and videos. It closes by highlighting community organizations leading recovery efforts, including My Tribe Rise, Evolve Altadena, and the Palisades Recovery Coalition.

The work was created by Rory Mitchell and Nonny de la Peña and co-produced by The Mercantile Agency, Emblematic Group, and Arizona State University's MA in Narrative and Emerging Media program, with support from Agog and the MacArthur Foundation.

Out of the Ashes assets: project page | press kit

About Empire at Sea

Empire at Sea is a 22-minute interactive augmented-reality drama about climate scientists building a sustainable community on a remote oil rig after a catastrophe cuts them off from the mainland. Up to 10 audience members experience cinematic holograms around a custom interactive LED table and navigate together a story about science, sustainability, immigration, and community.

The work was created, directed, and produced by Peter Flaherty; commissioned by Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts and ASU Gammage; developed with Flaherty Pictures, 4DV.ai, and NightLight Labs; and supported by Agog, the Schwarzman Center at Yale University, and the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation. It is scheduled to be presented at Lincoln Center in January 2027.

Empire at Sea assets: project page | website | press kit

Agog at Venice Immersive

Agog supported three projects selected for this year's Venice Immersive competition. The third, Solwata, is a mixed-reality documentary that brings audiences into the lives of communities in Solomon Islands confronting rising seas, displacement, and planned relocation. Created by NowHere Media and co-produced by Human Rights Watch and Agog, the experience is narrated and executive produced by Mark Ruffalo. Following its Venice premiere, Solwata is now being presented at the Toronto International Film Festival's Innovation Hub through Sept. 16. It will next appear at the BFI London Film Festival and COP31, the annual United Nations climate change conference.

Beyond its involvement with the three projects, Agog partnered with Venice Immersive on the occasion of the festival's 10th anniversary to shape discussions about what the next decade could hold, with a focus on impact. Throughout the festival, Agog convened creators, nonprofit leaders, funders, technologists, and cultural leaders for programming including a Smart Glasses Petting Zoo offering hands-on access to the latest emerging technology to consider ways it could be harnessed for storytelling and social good, an imagination workshop focused on expanding what is possible in immersive storytelling, and hands-on- conversations about new creative possibilities and the opportunities for immersive media to spur social change.

These activities are part of Agog's broader efforts to champion ambitious work, connect people across the immersive ecosystem, and help immersive media develop with public purpose at its center. Learn more

About Agog: The Immersive Media Institute

Agog: The Immersive Media Institute is a philanthropic organization founded by Chip Giller and Wendy Schmidt that is dedicated to helping creators and nonprofit leaders use immersive media—including virtual, augmented, and mixed reality—to imagine and build a more connected, just, and compassionate world. Agog operates as a field builder and creative partner, supporting immersive storytellers whose work addresses urgent social and environmental challenges. Learn more at agog.org

The Sonic Intelligence Academy unveils the SIQA Verified Registry and the SIQA Verified app, giving artists, industry, and fans a single source of truth for identifying AI music. LOS ANGELES, Sept. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SIQA (The Sonic Intelligence Academy Inc.), the independent data and verification platform for the AI music era backed by 1517 Fund, today announced the launch of the SIQA Verified Registry and the SIQA Verified app for iOS, unveiled through the company's Mid-Year AI Music Intelligence Report. The registry allows artists to register their work and gives the industry and the public a way to discover a track's origin and AI involvement.

SIQA operates the industry's first AI music charts, and this new registry extends that work, from ranking what's rising to verifying what's real. The company's guiding principle is simple: Verified, Not Flagged. Rather than policing or labeling tracks as suspect after the fact, SIQA equips artists to establish provenance up front, turning verification into a credential artists carry, not an accusation they have to defend against.

That distinction matters more than ever as AI-generated music floods streaming platforms like Spotify and Deezer faster than the industry can account for it, a shift now tracked by outlets from Billboard to Music Business Worldwide. The prevailing industry response has been reactive: identify AI tracks after release, then flag, dispute, or remove them. SIQA flips that model by verifying at the source, not flagging after the fact. The SIQA Verified Registry lets artists register and verify their work, while giving labels, distributors, DSPs, and everyday listeners a trusted way to check a track's provenance, going beyond the generic 'AI-Generated' label to classify each under the SIQA Classification Framework as Fully AI-Generated, AI-Assisted, or a Human + AI Hybrid (e.g., vocal cloning).

The SIQA Verified app identifies a song much like Shazam, and reveals its AI classification in seconds.

The companion SIQA Verified app puts that trust in your pocket. Much like Shazam identifies a song, SIQA Verified uses audio fingerprinting so anyone can discover a track's AI classification instantly, drawing on the SIQA Verified Registry to show whether a work is Fully AI-Generated, AI-Assisted, or a Human + AI Hybrid.

SIQA will also host the inaugural AI Music Awards (AIMAs) in Los Angeles on November 13, 2026 — a red-carpet celebration featuring celebrity appearances, the presentation of the first-ever SIQA Visionary Award, and live performances directed by the creators behind Xania Monet, Olivia B Moore, Chaisen Hale, EJ Rogers, and more.

The AI Music Awards are sponsored by a collective of music and tech companies including Deepgram, the real time voice infrastructure platform that powers conversational AI experiences for more than 1,300 companies, including Granola, Twilio, and Sierra.

"AI is rapidly expanding what's possible with sound and voice, which makes trust and transparency increasingly important," said Scott Stephenson, CEO of Deepgram. "We're excited to support SIQA in bringing creators, technologists, and the industry together to explore what responsible innovation can look like as this space evolves."

On November 12, the day before the awards, SIQA will host a summit (SIQA Summit) featuring panel discussions from bold, notable industry leaders of AI music, including Romel Murphy (CEO of dai+drm).

The SIQA Verified Registry is now live at registry.thesiqa.com, the Mid-Year AI Music Intelligence Report is available at thesiqa.com; the SIQA Verified app is available on the App Store.

About SIQA

SIQA (The Sonic Intelligence Academy Inc.) is an independent AI music intelligence and infrastructure company building the data, standards, and verification layer for the AI music era. Home to the industry's first AI music charts, SIQA operates on a simple principle: Verified, Not Flagged. The company is backed by 1517 Fund. Learn more at https://thesiqa.com

releases.body:
Fueled by Pocket FM, AI entertainment ecosystem features 550,000+ creators, doubles customer retention, and generates 2.6 million hours of content annually

CULVER CITY, Calif., Sept. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Pocket Entertainment, world's leading AI entertainment platform and the parent company of Pocket FM and Pocket Saga, today announced it has surpassed $500 million in Revenue Run Rate (ARR) growing 70% YOY.

The milestone reflects the continued global growth of Pocket FM, its flagship AI audio drama platform, alongside Pocket Entertainment's increasing use of AI across content creation, production, personalization and distribution.

"AI fundamentally changes the economics of entertainment businesses. Crossing $500 million in ARR, with a healthy bottom line, is a testament to that. Interestingly, Pocket FM has scaled while improving retention alongside it. That doesn't happen without having good taste." Harsha Kumar, Partner at Lightspeed.

Pocket FM remains the primary engine of Pocket Entertainment's growth. Revenue retention on the platform has increased from 44% to 76%, reflecting stronger and more sustained listener engagement. Strategic licensing and adaptation partnerships have further expanded its content offering, including a collaboration with Disney Publishing APAC that brought 36 iconic Marvel audio series episodes to Hindi-language listeners.

Over the past year, Pocket FM expanded into the UK, Germany and France, broadened its catalog across genres including Thriller and Fantasy, and launched user-generated content in the U.S., significantly increasing the volume and diversity of stories available to listeners.

This scale is translating into a growing portfolio of breakout franchises: 96 titles have each generated more than $1 million in revenue, including 13 that have surpassed $10 million.

Building an AI Entertainment Engine

Pocket FM brings together a global ecosystem of more than 550,000 creators, a purpose-built AI stack and real-time audience insights across creation, production, localization and distribution.

Real-time audience insights help identify stories that are resonating, enabling promising IP to scale faster across audiences and markets. AI reduces the time required to launch in new markets from approximately 12 months to two, allowing successful stories and IP to travel across languages and geographies far more quickly.

The result is a fundamentally different model for creating and scaling entertainment:

  • Pocket FM's creator ecosystem generates more than 2.6 million annualized hours of content.
  • The platform's library has grown to more than 770,000 titles across eight categories.
  • English-language originals and adaptations including Saving Nora, The Primal Hunter, The Duke's Masked Bride and Shadow Slave generate millions of plays, while My Vampire System surpassed 1.5 billion plays.

AI Is Opening Entertainment Creation to a New Generation of Storytellers

"AI is creating an entirely new era of entertainment, one defined by an abundance of high-quality content, the rise of single-person studios capable of creating blockbusters, and experiences hyper-personalized for every individual," said Rohan Nayak, CEO and Co-Founder of Pocket Entertainment. "We are already seeing creators build stories that generate millions of dollars, something that historically required large studios, big teams, significant budgets and years of production. We believe the next global entertainment phenomenon can come from anywhere, reach millions of people across the world, and still feel uniquely made for each of them. At Pocket Entertainment, we are building the platform for this future, fundamentally expanding who can create, what can be created, and how the world experiences entertainment."



Pocket FM listeners now spend an average of 155 minutes a day on the platform, with 51% of weekly active users engaging daily.

"I struggled to get my stories published, but now I can see them come to life with Pocket FM," said Steven Ade, writer and creator. "Pocket FM's AI creation tools help me develop ideas, build characters and storylines, and turn those ideas into stories much faster. I can spend more time being creative, create more consistently and see my stories reach audiences I never could before."

Pocket FM continues to welcome creators and writers from around the world to bring their stories to life and reach global audiences. To listen or start creating, visit pocketfm.com.

About Pocket FM

Pocket FM is the leading AI audio drama, shaping a new category of serialized entertainment for audiences around the world. With more than 250 million listeners across 20+ countries, Pocket FM combines human creativity and AI with audience insights to help more than 550,000 creators develop stories, produce audio, adapt content across languages and scale successful IP for global audiences. Pocket FM has built a rapidly growing library of more than 770,000 audio series, creating an entertainment ecosystem where creators can bring their ideas to life and reach audiences around the world. Pocket FM is headquartered in Bengaluru and Culver City, California, and is operated by parent company Pocket Entertainment.

About Pocket Entertainment

Pocket Entertainment is the world's leading AI entertainment platform building products that help creators create, produce, distribute and monetize entertainment at global scale. Its portfolio includes Pocket FM, the leading AI audio drama platform, and Pocket Saga, its AI microdrama platform. Founded in India in 2018 by Rohan Nayak, Nishanth KS and Prateek Dixit, Pocket Entertainment combines human creativity and AI to make audio and video entertainment creation faster and more accessible, enabling creators to develop high-quality entertainment, reach audiences across languages and geographies, and scale successful IP globally.

Pocket Entertainment is building a future of hyper-personalized entertainment, where individual creators can build global blockbusters that once required large studios, teams and budgets. Pocket Entertainment is headquartered in Bengaluru and Culver City, California, with offices in San Francisco, Berlin and Mumbai.

Contact:

Angela Baldwin

Pocket FM

releases.title: Korean Cultural Center New York presents Yunie's Magical Adventure: A Musical Dreamscape for the Whole Family
releases.body:
Friday, September 25, 2026 at 6 PM

Saturday, September 26, 2026 at 4 PM

Theater at the Korean Cultural Center New York

(North American Premiere) 

NEW YORK, Sept. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Korean Cultural Center New York (KCCNY), a branch of the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of the Republic of Korea, will present the North American premiere of Yunie's Magical Adventure: A Musical Dreamscape for the Whole Family for two performances on Friday, September 25 at 6 PM and Saturday, September 26 at 4 PM at the theater of the Korean Cultural Center New York as part of the "KCCNY Curates" series. Co-presented by KCCNY and MIRI Opera, the imaginative family music theater production blends live music, multimedia storytelling, and participatory play to create an engaging and interactive experience for young audiences and families.

Timed around Chuseok, often described as Korean Thanksgiving and one of Korea's most important traditional holidays, the production brings beloved Korean children's songs and traditional games to life through the vibrant sounds of Western classical and Korean traditional music. Through music, movement, and imaginative play, the performance celebrates the spirit of togetherness and shared memories while offering children and families a joyful introduction to Korean culture.

The story follows Yunie, a curious young girl who travels with her family to Grandma's house for Chuseok. While the adults are busy preparing the holiday feast, Yunie finds herself without anyone her age to play with. Just as she begins to feel lonely and sleepy, something extraordinary happens: tofu and bean sprouts come to life and become her new friends. Together, they enter a magical world filled with music, games, friendship, and unexpected discoveries.

Featuring a live chamber orchestra (New York Classical Players), colorful visuals, animation, and interactive storytelling, Yunie's Magical Adventure introduces audiences to some of Korea's most beloved traditional songs and games, including Kkomaya Kkomaya (Little Child), Mugunghwa Flower Has Bloomed (Korean Red Light, Green Light), Dong Dong Dongdaemun (Gate Game), Toad, Toad (Sandcastle Game), Hide-and-Seek, and Ganggangsullae (Circle Dance).

At its heart, Yunie's Magical Adventure explores universal themes of family, friendship, imagination, and belonging, creating a playful space where young audiences can discover Korean traditions while sharing the joy of music and play together.

Admission is free and open to the public, but pre-registration is required.

Synopsis

With Chuseok, one of Korea's most important traditional holidays, just around the corner, Yunie's family is busy shopping in a bustling marketplace. It is a cherished Korean tradition to make wishes under the full moon during Chuseok—but oh no, it's raining! Will Yunie and her family be able to see the full moon on Chuseok night?

On the morning of their trip to Grandma's house, cheerful Yunie sets off hand in hand with her loving mom and dad. But once they arrive, all the adults are busy preparing the holiday feast. With no other children her age around, Yunie begins to feel lonely and bored—and maybe even a little sleepy. Then, just as she is about to drift off, something extraordinary happens. Yunie's eyes open wide as a magical world begins to unfold before her!

Creative Team

Storyteller: Sung Yeena

Orchestra: New York Classical Players

Conductor: Kim Dongmin

Production: MIRI Opera

Original Story / Composition / Artistic Direction: Park Sungsun

Script: Yang Inyong & Chung Jooeun

Character Design / Animation / Media Art: Kim Hyeran

Storyteller Sung Yeena is a New York City–based actor, songwriter, and creative whose work spans theater, film, music, writing, and visual storytelling. Originally from South Korea, she is especially interested in stories of belonging and nuanced Korean and Korean American identity. Yeena holds an MFA from Columbia University and a BFA from NYU Tisch School of the Arts.

The production is led musically by New York Classical Players under conductor Kim Dongmin, with original story, composition, and artistic direction by Park Sungsun. The script is by Yang Inyong and Chung Jooeun, with character design, animation, and media art by Kim Hyeran. Together, the creative team combines live music, theatrical storytelling, and visual media to create an immersive world for young audiences.

About MIRI Opera Company

MIRI Opera Company is a creative and performing arts collective founded by artists who share a vision of building a "beautiful community" through the arts. Its parent organization, InterEduArt, was established in 2010, and the group has been active under the name MIRI Opera Company since 2017.

MIRI Opera Company oversees the entire creative process in-house—from performance planning and scriptwriting to composition and production—and has presented more than 200 performances across Korea. The company is also active in arts education through educational content development, teacher training programs, and professional consulting.

About New York Classical Players

New York Classical Players (NYCP) is a dynamic chamber orchestra redefining how classical music lives in our time. Founded in 2010 by music director Kim Dongmin, NYCP brings together exceptional musicians committed to artistic excellence, collaborative music-making, and meaningful engagement with audiences.

Through adventurous programming, commissions, premieres, recordings, and collaborations with leading artists, NYCP connects established repertoire with the music of the present. Based in the New York metropolitan area, the ensemble works closely with cultural institutions, presenters, and community partners to bring exceptional live music to audiences across New York City, northern New Jersey, and beyond.

About the Korean Cultural Center New York (KCCNY)

The Korean Cultural Center New York (KCCNY), a branch of the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of the Republic of Korea, was established in December 1979 to promote Korean culture and foster cultural exchange in New York. KCCNY presents a wide range of cultural and artistic programs, including exhibitions, performing arts, film, educational workshops, and more. At its home at 122 E 32nd Street in Manhattan, KCCNY serves as a cultural hub where audiences can discover and experience the richness of Korean culture.

About KCCNY Curates

KCCNY Curates is the flagship performance series of the Korean Cultural Center New York, dedicated to showcasing distinctive and innovative works of Korean performing arts in the heart of New York City. Launched in conjunction with KCCNY's theater, the series embodies the Center's curatorial vision by introducing exceptional productions that combine artistic excellence and creative exploration.

Featuring distinguished Korean artists and groundbreaking works across genres, KCCNY Curates offers New York audiences compelling opportunities to experience the dynamic spirit of Korea's performing arts scene and aims to establish itself as a signature platform for world-class Korean performing arts in New York.

For event details and RSVP, visit www.koreanculture.org and follow @kccny on Instagram.

For inquiries: Hyo Han (Program Director of Performing Arts), hhan@koreanculture.org

releases.body:
Bringing the Intact Prestige experience to the red carpet

TORONTO, Sept. 10, 2026 /CNW/ -- Intact Prestige, Intact Financial Corporation's specialized high-value insurance brand, is proud to announce a new partnership with the the Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF) supporting its iconic Beyond the Red Carpet Event, bringing Intact Prestige into the spotlight at one of the most celebrated cultural events in the world. The 51st edition of the festival kicks off today in Toronto and will celebrate the best of Canadian and global cinema over the next 10 days.

As part of the partnership, Intact Prestige will serve as the Presenting Partner of one of the Beyond the Red Carpet events, an exclusive event curated by TIFF's CEO Cameron Bailey, that brings the festival's most passionate supporters and industry leaders together to celebrate standout Gala Films. This year's event will take place on September 18, 2026 at the Ritz Carlton Toronto, followed by a Gala Premiere Screening of Wayne Wang's Diary of a Mad Old Man at Roy Thompson Hall. 

"Intact Prestige is always looking for meaningful ways to connect with the customers and brokers we serve, and there's no stage quite like TIFF," said Alyson Paisley, Deputy Senior Vice President, Intact Prestige. "Partnering with an event as iconic as TIFF's Beyond the Red Carpet puts the Intact Prestige brand exactly where it belongs - alongside excellence, distinction, and unforgettable moments. It's a natural fit for our customers, who like us, have an appreciation for creative and cultural experiences."

Intact Prestige is a bespoke offering for high-net-worth clients, combining specialized expertise, tailored coverage, and personalized service to meet each client's unique needs. To learn more about Intact Prestige visit www.intactprestige.com.

For more information on the Toronto International Film Festival, visit www.tiff.net.

About Intact Financial Corporation

Intact Financial Corporation (TSX: IFC) is a global provider of property and casualty insurance founded on core values and a belief that insurance is about people, not things. Intact's success is fueled by its 32,000 employees worldwide who embody the company's purpose: to help people, businesses and society prosper in good times and be resilient in bad times. To achieve its ambitions, Intact seeks to ensure customers are its advocates, its people are engaged, and the company is one of the most respected. 

Intact is the largest provider of property and casualty insurance in Canada and has successfully exported its strengths across North America, the UK and Europe. Its growing commercial and specialty solutions network now spans over 150 countries. With a customer-driven mindset, Intact has expanded its operations to include insurance distribution, restoration, and prevention.

Intact solidifies its outperformance by leveraging its competitive advantages: global leadership in data and AI for pricing and risk selection; deep claims expertise and integrated supply chain network; and strong capital and investment management. Intact's total annual operating Direct Premiums Written has tripled over the last decade to $25 billion. Explore Intact's offerings at intactfc.com.

Great American Christmas, one of the most anticipated holiday events on television, continues its sixth season with an extraordinary collection of Original movies pairing the genre's most beloved stars with stories made to become Christmas traditions.

Merritt Patterson and Ryan Paevey Star in The Ornament Library, a Great American Christmas Original 2026 movie.

In The Ornament Library, meticulous librarian Alice Montgomery (Patterson) and newspaper reporter Noah Conrad (Paevey) discover a forgotten room hidden beneath their town's historic library, filled with hundreds of Christmas ornaments containing handwritten memories from generations past. As they set out to reunite each treasured keepsake with its rightful family, the pair rekindles a cherished Christmas tradition, strengthen an entire community, and discover that the greatest gifts of the season are the stories – and people – we carry in our hearts.

"The Ornament Library is a great story with tremendous talent as Merritt Patterson and Ryan Paevey create the kind of emotional connection that brings audiences back year after year," said Kaitlyn Haubrich, Chief Brand Officer and Chief of Staff, Great American Media. This is the standard we are setting for Great American Christmas," Haubrich concluded.

The Ornament Library is written by Ainsley Gordon.

releases.title: UNIVERSAL MUSIC GROUP AND ELEVENLABS ANNOUNCE MULTI-YEAR STRATEGIC AGREEMENT, BEGINNING WITH A NEW LICENSED AI MUSIC CREATION PLATFORM
releases.body:
First-of-its-kind collaboration spans licensing and product development  

New platform, to be launched by ElevenLabs, will enable fans to create remixes, mashups and new interpretations of tracks from participating artists 

SANTA MONICA, Calif. and NEW YORK, Sept. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Universal Music Group (UMG), the world leader in music-based entertainment, and ElevenLabs, the leading AI audio research and product company, today announced a multi-year licensing agreement and wider strategic collaboration to launch a new AI-powered music platform for fans as well as to jointly develop AI audio products for artists and songwriters.  

The groundbreaking agreement – ElevenLabs' first with a major label – encompasses licensing and product development. It reflects the companies' shared commitment to the principles that AI-enabled music innovation should be built responsibly, respect human artistry, and enable artists and songwriters to share in the value created.  

The ElevenLabs-UMG relationship will begin with a new AI-powered music creation platform built on licensed music and artist participation. Now in development, the platform will give fans new ways to co-create with music from participating artists and songwriters, including through remixes and mashups, new track interpretations, and personalized vocal experiences. The agreement also includes the development of additional products and fan experiences in the months and years to come. 

"The most exciting possibilities for AI and music are those that put artists, songwriters, and fans at the center," said Sir Lucian Grainge, Chairman & CEO, Universal Music Group. "UMG and ElevenLabs are aligned that responsible AI can inspire discovery, deepen engagement between artists and fans, and unlock new revenue opportunities for the creative community. ElevenLabs' leadership in AI audio brings a new dimension to our growing ecosystem of partners committed to expanding what's creatively and commercially possible for human artistry." 

"AI opens up incredible possibilities for interacting with our favorite music and artists," said ElevenLabs cofounder and CEO Mati Staniszewski. "By combining UMG's global community and rights management expertise, with our AI models and products, we'll enable artists and songwriters to create powerful new experiences for their fans, and ensure they are fairly compensated."   

The new platform will be distinct and offered separately from ElevenLabs' existing music products, which include: 

  • Music API – ElevenLabs' studio-grade music models available via API, used by music technology, media & entertainment, social media, and other leading businesses and developers globally. 
  • ElevenMusic – ElevenLabs' music creation app for generating and editing original songs, with granular control over vocals, instrumentation, style, arrangement and other elements of a track. 

About Universal Music Group

At Universal Music Group, we exist to shape culture through the power of artistry. UMG is the world leader in music-based entertainment, with a broad array of businesses engaged in recorded music, music publishing, merchandising and audiovisual content. Featuring the most comprehensive catalogue of recordings and songs across every musical genre, UMG identifies and develops artists and produces and distributes the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful music in the world. Committed to artistry, innovation and entrepreneurship, UMG fosters the development of services, platforms and business models in order to broaden artistic and commercial opportunities for our artists and create new experiences for fans. For more information on Universal Music Group N.V. visit www.universalmusic.com. 

About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company. It builds AI voice and audio models, creative tools, and conversational agents across 70+ languages. Millions of consumers, developers, governments, and businesses use ElevenLabs – including employees at two-thirds of Fortune 500 companies. With its models and platform, the company aims to transform how people and businesses communicate with the world.

releases.title: Shania Twain And Zedd Give "You're Still The One" A Sweet Reimagining For Candy Crush's Music Season 2026
releases.body:
An interactive Candy Country music experience invites fans to explore the track and unlock rewards, including VIP trips to meet the artists on tour

NEW YORK, Sept. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Candy Crush® is bringing together globally celebrated songwriter, artist and performer Shania Twain and Grammy Award-winning DJ and producer Zedd to give nearly 30 years of nostalgia a whole new sound. Today, the casual mobile game kicks off its annual Music Season in-game event with a candy-coated, dancefloor-ready reimagining of the song, "You're Still the One."

The track sets the pace to an interactive music video that transports fans to Candy Country — a glittering, candy-coated Western fantasy world where it rains rhinestones, roadhouse saloons shimmer like gumdrops and rainbow rapids rush in technicolor. Directed by acclaimed filmmaker Jonas Åkerlund, the video brings his distinctive visual storytelling to the Candy Crush Saga universe, transforming the game's playful spirit into a world filled with surreal moments. Look a little closer and fans will find hidden clues throughout the video that could unlock a range of prizes.

Fans can head to candyroadhouse.com to enter, seek out the blue sugar stars, and hunt for rewards.* The stakes are high with six lucky winners scoring a VIP trip to meet Shania Twain or Zedd on tour. Fans can also get their hands on signed bandanas and one-of-a-kind pieces straight out of the music video itself, including Shania's baby pink hero outfit with fringe detail as well as Zedd's rhinestone-encrusted helmet.

At the center of it all is a gift to the fans who've loved this song for thirty years: Shania Twain's timeless vocals, with Zedd's genre-blending production, riding straight through Candy Country's glittering desert world.

"Bringing 'You're Still The One' back with Zedd, and building this special world with Candy Crush for fans to play in, felt like the perfect way to give the song new life. It feels exactly right," said Shania Twain.

"I was super happy Candy Crush brought me and Shania Twain together. She's a legendary artist, and I grew up listening to her music, so being able to collaborate with her on a new version of such an iconic song has been really special," said Zedd.

Last year, Candy Crush teamed up with Thundercat to reimagine a renowned Diana Ross track as a playable, swipe-driven music video. This year evolves that experience even further, turning a music video into an interactive hunt for hidden codes, surprises, and rewards. It's a natural evolution for a brand built around play, turning passive viewing into active discovery and creating new ways for fans to engage.

"Candy Crush has always been about making everyday moments more fun. Music Season takes that spirit into music culture, turning a song people know and love into something they can explore, play with and share. Working with Shania and Zedd gives fans a fresh experience and another way to experience Candy Crush beyond the game," said Luken Aragon, Chief Marketing Officer, King.

Music Season 2026 tournament is now live in-game through October 5, 2026, with the Music Season Expedition available from level 11 onward. Fans can also watch the video and start uncovering hidden rewards at candyroadhouse.com. Follow @candycrushsaga on Instagram and TikTok for live updates and Easter egg clues.

Candy Crush Saga® is free to download on iOS and Android. For more information, visit candycrushsaga.com.

*candyroadhouse.com rewards are available to U.S. residents only.

About Candy Crush Saga

Candy Crush Saga® is one of the world's most popular mobile games. Millions of players around the globe match colorful candies in combinations of three or more to win points, defeat obstacles, and progress through more than 20,000 levels. In November 2022, Candy Crush Saga celebrated its 10-year anniversary. Candy Crush Saga is available to download for free from the Apple App Store, Google Play, Amazon App Store, Windows App Store and Facebook.

About King

With a mission of Making the World Playful, King is a leading interactive entertainment company for the mobile world with more than 20 years of history of delivering some of the world's most iconic games in the mobile gaming industry, including the world-famous Candy Crush franchise, as well as other mobile titles such as Farm Heroes Saga. Around 200 million people play a King game every month. King, part of Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), has Kingsters in Stockholm, Malmö, London, Barcelona, Berlin, Dublin, San Francisco, New York, Los Angeles and Malta. More information can be found at King.com or by following us on LinkedIn and @lifeatking on Instagram.

About Shania Twain

Shania Twain is a five-time GRAMMY Award-winning artist, songwriter, and performer who helped redefine country music for a global audience with her genre-blending, boundary-pushing sound. With seven studio albums and more than 100 million records sold worldwide, she remains the top-selling female country-pop artist of all time, behind era-defining hits like "You're Still The One," "Man! I Feel Like A Woman!," and "That Don't Impress Me Much." Her latest album, Little Miss Twain, blends country, pop, rock, soul, and Motown influences with collaborators including Tanya Tucker, Ronnie Wood, and Josh Homme. releases.body:
New two-day interactive festival at Peoria Civic Center features a $50,000 Collegiate Esports Showdown, hands-on gaming and entertainment experiences, plus Future Play After Dark with Lil Jon and James Hype

PEORIA, Ill., Sept. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- This October, the future of entertainment is coming to Peoria — and audiences won't just watch it. They'll play it.

Future Play Festival, an all-new interactive gaming, esports, entertainment and technology experience, takes over the Peoria Civic Center October 3–4, 2026, bringing together competitive gaming, immersive attractions, creators, music and hands-on experiences for one action-packed weekend.

Unlike a traditional convention where attendees spend the day walking past exhibits, Future Play is built to be experienced.

Fans can step inside interactive attractions, compete and play, experience new technology, watch some of the country's top collegiate esports competitors battle live, meet creators, race RC cars, rediscover classic arcade games, experience live entertainment — and Saturday night, turn up with Lil Jon and James Hype at Future Play After Dark.

Tickets are on sale now, with festival admission starting at just $19.99.

"Future Play was created around a simple idea: don't just come and watch — come and play, compete and experience it for yourself," said Dylan Marer, Executive Producer at Cinematic, LLC., the producer of Future Play Festival. "We're bringing gaming, esports, immersive entertainment, technology and live music together under one roof to create a completely different kind of weekend experience. We want people to walk through the doors and continually discover something new."

$50,000 COLLEGIATE ESPORTS SHOWDOWN

At the center of Future Play will be the Future Play Collegiate Esports Showdown, where collegiate competitors will battle live for a $50,000 Rocket League prize pool.

The tournament brings the excitement of competitive collegiate esports out from behind the screen and onto the live stage, giving fans the opportunity to experience the speed, strategy and intensity of high-level Rocket League competition in person.

But the competition is only part of the experience.

THIS ISN'T JUST A SHOW. IT'S A PLAYGROUND.

Across the Peoria Civic Center, Future Play will give attendees an entire weekend of things to play, try, explore and experience, including:

  • Airsoft Tactical Shoot House Experience
  • EVIKE.com Airsoft Shooting Range
  • ARRMA RC Racing Experiences
  • Retro Arcade Gaming Lounge
  • Creator Studio
  • Immersive and emerging technology experiences
  • Live DJs and entertainment
  • Cosplay
  • Celebrity gaming appearances
  • Interactive gaming and brand activations
  • Future Play Collegiate Esports Showdown
  • And more experiences throughout the weekend

Whether you're a serious gamer, college student, esports fan, creator, tech enthusiast, music fan, parent introducing your kids to the games you grew up playing — or simply looking for something completely different to do — Future Play is designed to offer an experience for you.

"Most events stay in one lane," Marer said. "There are gaming conventions. There are esports tournaments. There are technology shows. And there are concerts. Future Play brings all of those worlds together and makes the audience part of the experience."

WHEN THE SUN GOES DOWN, FUTURE PLAY GOES AFTER DARK

The experience gets even bigger Saturday night.

On Saturday, October 3, Future Play transforms for Future Play After Dark, an explosive live music experience featuring hip-hop icon Lil Jon and global electronic music star James Hype.

From 8:00–11:30 p.m., the energy moves from the gaming floor to the concert experience as two internationally recognized artists bring Future Play's opening day to a high-energy finale.

Festival guests can choose from festival-only, concert-only and combination ticket options, making it possible to build their own Future Play weekend.

For fans looking for the complete experience, two-day festival + Future Play After Dark packages offer the best way to experience the entire weekend.

PEORIA BECOMES THE PLACE TO PLAY

Future Play is also part of a larger effort to establish Peoria as a Midwest destination for esports, emerging entertainment and next-generation live experiences.

"Peoria has been intentional in recruiting and investing in cutting-edge entertainment and event segments that bring world-class talent, new audiences and increased visitation to our region," said JD Dalfonso, CEO of Discover Peoria.

"One way we are doing this is by bolstering our efforts in esports and the entertainment opportunities that come with this rapidly growing industry. Future Play represents an exciting next step in that work. It will bring visitors from across the country to experience Peoria, while showcasing our community as a destination willing to embrace new ideas, new audiences and new forms of entertainment."

Dalfonso added, "We see this inaugural event as the beginning of something much bigger for esports, tourism and the region, and we are proud to be part of what comes next."

releases.body:
VENICE, Italy, Sept. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Tamar AI, the Palo Alto-based AI-powered creative technology company behind TapNow, the world's first AI-native Creative OS, today announced the launch of Glanze at the 83rd Venice Film Festival. As a streaming platform for original AI-native series, films, and explorable worlds, Glanze extends the TapNow ecosystem, creating a single connected path from creation to global audience.

Powered by TapNow and fed by its global IP incubation initiative 10,000 Parallel Universes, Glanze is a streaming platform built to redefine how stories are discovered, turning the exploration of original works into part of the entertainment experience. With Glanze now live, locally rooted AI-native series and films are brought to global audiences without the limits of traditional streaming platforms. Glanze opens with 40 titles available for preview, enabling creativity to travel without boundaries.

"Debuting Glanze at Venice, one of the world's most prestigious film festivals and where the future of cinema is first seen, marks our ambition to establish AI as a creative and meaningful force in the global film industry. Glanze is not just a streaming platform but an integral part of the TapNow ecosystem, rooted in our belief that AI exists to amplify creation from idea to distribution," said Klaus He, Co-founder of Tamar AI.

The Glanze launch was accompanied by a panel co-hosted by TapNow during the Venice Film Festival's Venice Production Bridge on September 4. The "AI x Cinema: The 10,000 Parallel Universes Initiative" panel brought together AI filmmakers, industry leaders and film educators to explore AI's creative and economic impact on filmmaking. The session closed with a technical presentation of "Primodia," a flagship series from the 10,000 Parallel Universes initiative, to showcase TapNow's Creative OS in action. On September 7, a curated screening of selected AI-native stories from the initiative offered a first look of the original worlds that Glanze is built to bring to global audiences.

Venice marks the beginning of a broader season of activity for Tamar AI, which will next bring its AI filmmaking community to Japan and Korea for Arena Peak Asia, its proprietary creator hackathon focused on cross-border AI storytelling, in October 16 - 19.

About Tamar AI

Tamar AI is a global AI-powered creative technology company headquartered in Palo Alto, California, built on the belief that AI should amplify the creator, not replace them. Its flagship product, TapNow, the world's first AI-native Creative OS, powers an ecosystem spanning tools, community, talent development, production, education, and distribution, forming a continuous path from first idea to finished work, from creator community to global audience. Trusted by creators across 150+ countries and regions, Tamar AI supports creators at every stage of the creative lifecycle through AI Creation System, AI-native Creator ecosystem, and Glanze – the streaming platform for original AI-native IPs.

releases.title: MANN ROBINSON EXPANDS ENTERTAINMENT ECOSYSTEM WITH 'URBAN OPERAS', A NEW VERTICAL STREAMING PLATFORM BUILT FOR STORIES THAT KNOW US
releases.body:
Urban Operas will launch with 15 original micro dramas produced by Robinson and his production team, while creating a new streaming destination for independent vertical filmmakers

ATLANTA, Sept. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Filmmaker, director, producer, studio owner, distributor, and streaming entrepreneur Mann Robinson is expanding his growing entertainment ecosystem with the launch of Urban Operas, a new vertical streaming platform created to bring culturally connected, mobile first storytelling directly to audiences.

Built around the tagline, "Stories That Know Us", Urban Operas will feature serialized dramas created specifically for mobile viewing, with short, fast moving episodes built around compelling characters, emotional storytelling, cliffhangers, relationships, romance, crime, family, betrayal, ambition, money, power, and the experiences of audiences that Robinson believes remain underserved within the rapidly expanding vertical entertainment marketplace.

Urban Operas is not being created in opposition to the major companies already operating in the vertical entertainment space. Instead, he sees this as an opportunity to expand the marketplace by creating a platform with a specific cultural identity and programming philosophy. When speaking of what makes Urban Operas unique, Robinson says, "The major platforms have their audiences and the types of programming that make sense for their businesses. I respect that. I saw an opportunity to build something from our perspective. There should be a destination where our stories aren't simply another category somewhere inside the platform. They are the foundation of the platform. That's what Urban Operas is being built to become. Original content will remain at the center of Urban Operas."

Independent filmmakers can find submission details through the official Urban Operas website at www.urbanoperas.com. Selected outside productions will have the opportunity to be distributed through Urban Operas under a creator focused revenue share model, allowing qualified filmmakers and content owners to participate financially in the performance of their programming on the platform.

Urban Operas will begin appearing on the Apple App Store and Google Play Store in November 2026, with its official launch scheduled for Winter 2026.

ABOUT MANN ROBINSON

Mann Robinson has produced and directed more than 30 film and television projects and has built an independent entertainment operation spanning film and television production, content distribution, production equipment, marketing, props and production resources, and direct to consumer streaming.

BEND, Ore., Sept. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hydro Flask®, an award-winning leader in high-performance insulated products, and singer-songwriter Role Model (Tucker Pillsbury) have teamed up to launch a Limited Edition collection of reusable drinkware inspired by his third studio album, Chuck Timely & The Hourglass. The eight-piece collection marks the second drop in a series of artist-inspired products released through the Hydro Flask x Universal Music Group (UMG) partnership. The partnership brings reusable hydration into music culture, aimed at reducing single-use beverage waste across UMG's global studios, songwriting sessions and live events.  

Hydro Flask and Role Model Launch Reusable Drinkware Collection

The collection is available today, coinciding with the start of Role Model Presents: Chuck On Tour, which kicks off in Hydro Flask's hometown of Bend, Oregon. To mark the launch, Hydro Flask and Role Model debuted a promotional spot that continues to showcase Role Model's talents beyond music. Filmed alongside longtime friend and creative collaborator Ky Newman, the playful campaign gives fans a glimpse of the duo's natural comedic chemistry while spotlighting the artist's Hydro Flask collection.

"Being able to outfit the whole band and crew with reusable bottles cuts down on waste to really make an impact while we're on the road," said Role Model. "We also got to run with the creative for this campaign, so it just felt like me and Ky doing what we normally do."

"Hydro Flask has always led with joy. Role Model brings that same spirit to music, and our partnership was a natural fit," said Larry Witt, Hydro Flask President. "Since launching our partnership with UMG, we've seen a strong response from fans and artists. Our new campaign with Role Model shows that reusables can be part of everyday life, and that making a positive impact can be simple, easy, and even a little fun."

Role Model x Hydro Flask Collection

The Limited Edition collection includes eight Hydro Flask bottles, selected and designed in partnership with Role Model. Colors and printed or engraved graphic elements throughout the collection draw from the visual identity of Chuck Timely & The Hourglass. 

The collection includes variations of top-selling Hydro Flask bottles, the 32 oz Wide Flex Straw Cap, 24 oz Wide Flex Straw Cap and 400mL Micro Hydro. All bottles in the collection also include matching boots for extra bump and ding protection. 

The Role Model x Hydro Flask collection is available now on HydroFlask.com, with pricing ranging from $37.95 to $49.95 USD.       

About Role Model

Role Model (Tucker Pillsbury) has emerged as one of pop music's most compelling singer-songwriters, building a devoted global following through his deeply personal songwriting, genre-bending sound, and magnetic personality. His third album, Chuck Timely & The Hourglass, was released August 7 and marks an exciting new chapter for the platinum-certified artist. The album's lead single, "High Hopes 3000," became Role Model's first entry on the Billboard Hot 100, while the album debuted in the Top 10 of the Billboard 200. 

About Hydro Flask

Hydro Flask, a Helen of Troy Limited (Nasdaq: HELE) brand, was founded in 2009 with the goal of delivering high-performance, reusable insulated products to help people enjoy the things they like to do in the places they like to be. Dedicated to eliminating single-use plastics, the company is a leader in award-winning double-wall insulated bottles, tumblers, mugs and coolers. To learn more about Hydro Flask and to see the company's full lineup of award-winning products, visit hydroflask.com.

Featuring the most comprehensive catalogue of recordings and songs across every musical genre, UMG identifies and develops artists and produces and distributes the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful music in the world. releases.body:
Dashverse's AI storytelling agent Frameo outperformed 8 leading AI filmmaking agents, scoring 88.7, nearly 20 points ahead of the runner-up and ranking first across Narrative Coherence, Cinematic Language and Production Quality.

  • Frameo ranked #1 on 13 of 16 metrics, including all 8 human-preference metrics, in a 100-prompt, 800-video human evaluation.

SAN FRANCISCO and BENGALURU, India, Sept. 9, 2026 /CNW/ -- Dashverse today announced that Frameo, its AI filmmaking and video generation agent, ranked #1 in Arc v1.0 Movie, an independent benchmark published by Physion Labs. In a human evaluation of 8 AI video agents, including Runway Agent 2.0, Luma Creative Agents, Kling Canvas Agent, and Invideo Agent One, Frameo scored 88.7 out of 100 on quality, nearly twenty points clear of the second-placed agent.

"The margin was large enough that it caught us by surprise. We ran a round of validation and brought in a fourth expert reviewer. The conclusion held: the results are valid, and Frameo is meaningfully ahead of every other agent that we evaluated," said Qin Zhang, Founder and CEO of Physion Labs.

Frameo was not built to win filmmaking benchmarks

Dashverse Co-Founder and CTO Soumyadeep Mukherjee built Frameo as the production system behind the company's AI short dramas that consumers pay to watch.

"We never optimized Frameo for movies. We built it for short dramas that audiences pay for, so the #1 result surprised us too," said Soumyadeep Mukherjee, CTO of Dashverse. "The benchmark has opened up a whole new world of possibilities, from ads to films. We're already seeing studios, brands, and creators reach out to explore what they can create with Frameo."

From short dramas to film, television, and marketing

Following these results, Dashverse is expanding Frameo beyond short dramas into film, television, and marketing. The company will work with studios, OTTs and brands, combining Frameo with trained Dashverse artists via its Forward Deployed Artist (FDA) model.

"The benchmark showed us that the system we built to run our own shows is now one of the strongest AI filmmaking systems in the world," said Sanidhya Narain, CEO of Dashverse.

About Dashverse

Dashverse is an AI-native entertainment company operating from San Francisco and Bengaluru. Its AI short dramas are watched by paying audiences worldwide and produced by 500+ trained AI artists using Frameo, its AI filmmaking agent.

releases.title: From Classrooms to Festival Stages: Toyota and Music Will Empower the Next Generation of Artists
releases.body:
Toyota Donates $75,000 and Provides Students with Real-World Festival Experiences

PLANO, Texas, Sept. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Music has the power to inspire creativity, build confidence and strengthen communities. Through its continued partnership with Music Will, the nation's largest nonprofit music education program, Toyota is helping bring those opportunities to more students through a $75,000 donation and a series of unforgettable real-world experiences that connect them beyond the classroom.

Experience the full interactive Multichannel News Release here: https://www.multivu.com/conill_toyota/9419551-en-toyota-music-will-nonprofit-music-education-program-partnership

This year, Toyota and Music Will partnered through the Driving Music Forward initiative, a purpose-driven program designed to support music education, uplift diverse voices and inspire the next generation of artists through authentic, real-world opportunities. The initiative brings together Toyota's music platform, nonprofit partnerships and festival activations under a unified effort focused on community impact through music.

"Organizations like Music Will demonstrate the powerful role music plays in education and community engagement," said Paul Doleshal, general manager, motorsports and sponsorships, Toyota. "Through this initiative, we're connecting purpose-driven storytelling with tangible action, creating opportunities that allow students to perform and grow. Whether it's a classroom experience or a performance on a festival stage, we are proud to support programs that make a measurable difference in young people's lives."

The $75,000 donation will support music education programs in communities connected to Music Will and Toyota's music activations, helping ensure students have access to the instruments, resources and opportunities needed to develop their talents. Toyota's partnership with Music Will extends beyond financial support by creating meaningful experiences that help students see what's possible through music.

"As we enter year two of our partnership, Toyota's continued commitment is making a profound impact on modern music programs in public school classrooms nationwide," said Janice Polizzotto, Chief Growth Officer, Music Will. "By pairing this ongoing support with once-in-a-lifetime, real-world festival opportunities, we're giving students an unforgettable platform for creativity, confidence, and self-expression. Together, we're helping youth thrive by showing them that their passion and potential truly matter."

Throughout the year, students participating in Music Will programs experienced some of the nation's biggest festivals, performing on the Toyota Music Den stage, including Sueños Music Festival in Chicago, Roots Picnic in Philadelphia, Lollapalooza in Chicago and Head In The Clouds in Los Angeles. These performances gave students invaluable exposure to live audiences and the unique experience of participating in nationally recognized music festivals.

By providing students the opportunity to showcase their talent, Toyota is helping bridge the gap between education and opportunity while celebrating the cultural expression that music makes possible. The initiative aligns with Toyota's broader commitment to creating positive community impact through programs that empower future generations and foster meaningful connections through shared experiences.

About Toyota 

Toyota (NYSE:TM) has been a part of the cultural fabric in the North America for nearly 70 years, and is committed to advancing sustainable, next-generation mobility through our Toyota and Lexus brands, plus our nearly 1,800 dealerships. 

Toyota directly employs nearly 64,000 people in North America who have contributed to the design, engineering, and assembly of more than 50 million cars and trucks at our 14 manufacturing plants. In 2025, Toyota's plant in North Carolina began to assemble automotive batteries for electrified vehicles.

For more information about Toyota, visit www.ToyotaNewsroom.com.

About Music Will

Music Will's mission is to transform lives by transforming music education. Through its innovative modern band curriculum, Music Will expands student participation in school music programs and helps drive long-term academic, social, and emotional growth. Since 2002, the organization has provided teacher training, curriculum, and instruments to over 6,000 schools across all 50 states, reaching more than 1.8 million students to date.

The program's roots go back to 1996, when a classroom teacher in East Palo Alto, CA, began offering free guitar lessons to his students to fill the gap left by the absence of a music program at his school. What started in one elementary classroom has since grown into a national movement, expanding to more than 1,000 school districts nationwide. By 2030, Music Will aims to reach 11 million students annually through its nationally scaled programming.
